related_questions.question: How does Loa loa affect the body?
related_questions.snippet: Loa loa is a parasitic filarial nematode that infects human skin and eyes with probable allergic offset, resulting in kidney, lung, and heart disease. It has affected human beings for ages: the earliest reliable documentation was in 1770 in the Carribean. Today it is a disease of Equatorial, West, and East Africa.

related_questions.question: Can Loa loa be cured?
related_questions.snippet: Medications. The drug of choice for the treatment of loiasis is diethylcarbamazine (DEC). Most patients will achieve cure, defined as resolution of symptoms, resolution of eosinophilia, and decreasing antifilarial antibody titers, with one or two courses of DEC.

text_blocks.snippet: Loa loa worm infection, also known as loiasis or African eye worm, can cause various symptoms, the most common being itchy swellings under the skin (Calabar swellings) and the sensation of a worm crawling across the eye. While many infected individuals are asymptomatic, those who experience symptoms may also have fatigue, joint pain, and general itching.
snippet_highlighted_words: itchy swellings under the skin (Calabar swellings) and the sensation of a worm crawling across the eye

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed breakdown of the symptoms:

list.snippet: Calabar swellings: These are localized, itchy, and non-pitting swellings that appear on the limbs, often near joints. They are a reaction to the worm and its metabolic products.

Eye worm (subconjunctival migration): The worm can be seen crawling under the conjunctiva (the transparent membrane covering the white part of the eye), which can cause irritation, pain, and a foreign body sensation.
General itching: Some individuals experience itching all over their body.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or weak is another potential symptom.
Joint pain: Pain in the joints may also occur.
Less common symptoms: Some individuals may experience muscle pain, and in rare cases, dead worms can cause chronic abscesses.
